subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: UK mains supply has an rms voltage of about 230 V. Its approximate peak voltage is:
When a capacitor discharges through a resistor, the charge follows:
questions.explain: Discharge is exponential decay: Q = Q₀e^(−t/RC).

questions.q: In an ideal (100% efficient) transformer, the relationship between primary and secondary power is:
questions.explain: With 100% efficiency the input power equals the output power: V_p I_p = V_s I_s.

questions.q: The farad (F) is equivalent to:
questions.explain: From C = Q/V, the farad equals one coulomb per volt (C V⁻¹).

questions.q: After one time constant during discharge, the charge on a capacitor falls to approximately:
questions.explain: After t = RC, Q = Q₀e⁻¹ ≈ 0.37Q₀, i.e. about 37% of the initial value.

questions.q: An ideal transformer steps voltage up from 240 V to 12 kV. If the primary current is 50 A, the secondary current is:
questions.explain: V_p I_p = V_s I_s, so I_s = (240 × 50)/12000 = 1.0 A; stepping voltage up steps current down.

questions.q: A common use of a capacitor is:
options: to generate a magnetic field permanently
to smooth a rectified voltage in a power supply
questions.explain: Capacitors store charge and release it to smooth ripple in rectified DC supplies.

questions.q: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor. The thumb, first finger and second finger represent, respectively:
questions.explain: In the left-hand rule, the thumb is force (motion), first finger is field, and second finger is current (F-B-I).

questions.q: The magnetic flux density B has the SI unit:
questions.explain: Magnetic flux density is measured in tesla; 1 T = 1 Wb m⁻².

questions.q: A magnet is dropped north-pole-down through a vertical coil. As it approaches, the induced current in the coil makes the top of the coil a:
options: north pole, to repel the magnet
south pole, to attract the magnet
north pole, to attract the magnet
south pole, to repel the magnet
questions.explain: By Lenz's law the coil opposes the approaching north pole by presenting a north pole to repel it.

questions.q: Lenz's law is fundamentally a consequence of the conservation of:
questions.explain: If the induced current aided the change, energy would be created from nothing; opposing the change conserves energy.

questions.q: A transformer's iron core is laminated (made of thin insulated sheets) primarily to:
options: reduce energy losses due to eddy currents
questions.explain: Laminating the core breaks up the paths for eddy currents, reducing the energy they would otherwise dissipate as heat.

questions.q: Electric potential at a point is the work done per unit positive charge in bringing it from:
questions.explain: Electric potential V is the work done per unit positive charge moving it from infinity to the point.

questions.q: A 2.0 µF capacitor discharges through a 1.0 MΩ resistor. The time constant is:
An ideal transformer has 100 turns on the primary and 500 turns on the secondary. If the primary voltage is 12 V, the secondary voltage is:
questions.explain: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p, so V_s = 12 × 500/100 = 60 V (a step-up transformer).

questions.q: An electron (charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) moves at 2.0 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ perpendicular to a 0.50 T field. The magnetic force on it is:
A sinusoidal AC has a peak current of 4.0 A. The average power it dissipates in a resistor equals that of a steady DC current of:
questions.explain: The equivalent DC is the rms current: I_rms = I_peak/√2 = 4.0/1.414 ≈ 2.83 A.

questions.q: The force on a charge q moving with velocity v at right angles to a field B is given by:
questions.explain: The magnetic force on a moving charge is F = Bqv when v is perpendicular to B.

questions.q: Equipotentials around a point charge are:
questions.explain: Equipotentials around a point charge form concentric spheres, perpendicular to the radial field lines.

questions.q: The charge stored on a 470 µF capacitor at 9.0 V is:
A charged oil drop of charge q is held stationary between horizontal plates. The electric force on it equals:
questions.explain: For equilibrium the electric force qE balances the weight mg.

questions.q: Lenz's law states that the direction of an induced current is always such that it:
options: enhances the change in flux that produced it
opposes the change in flux that produced it
is independent of the flux change
questions.explain: The induced current opposes the change causing it, which is why Faraday's law carries a minus sign.

questions.q: A capacitor is fully charged and connected to a steady DC supply. The current flowing onto it is then:
questions.explain: Once fully charged, no further charge flows, so the current is zero in steady state.

questions.q: The field lines between two oppositely charged parallel plates are:
options: parallel and evenly spaced (except at the edges)
questions.explain: A uniform field is represented by parallel, equally spaced lines, with fringing only at the edges.

questions.q: For a charged particle of mass m and charge q moving at speed v perpendicular to field B, the radius of its circular path is:
questions.explain: Setting Bqv = mv²/r gives r = mv/(Bq).

questions.q: The electric field strength a distance r from a point charge Q is:
questions.explain: E = F/q = Q/(4πε₀r²), a radial inverse-square field.

questions.q: The National Grid transmits power at very high voltage mainly to:
options: reduce the current for a given power, lowering I²R heating losses in the cables
increase the current and so the power delivered
increase the resistance of the cables
questions.explain: For a given power, higher voltage means lower current, and since power loss in cables is I²R, lower current greatly reduces resistive heating losses.

questions.q: Capacitance is defined as:
questions.explain: Capacitance C = Q/V, the charge stored per unit potential difference.

questions.q: In a simple AC generator, the peak EMF is induced when the coil is:
options: perpendicular to the field, enclosing maximum flux
parallel to the field (plane of coil along the field), cutting flux fastest
questions.explain: Peak EMF occurs when the coil's plane is parallel to the field, so the rate of change of flux linkage (flux cutting) is greatest.

questions.q: To increase the time constant of an RC discharge circuit, you could:
questions.explain: Since τ = RC, increasing either resistance or capacitance increases the time constant.
